bug_semantics: A BASIC app user who is allowed to execute a builder-created MongoDB query can supply a parameter containing quotes, duplicate JSON keys, and MongoDB $-operators. The query runner interpolated that value into a string-form json/customData/requestBody template with Handlebars escaping forcibly disabled and only then called JSON.parse. The value therefore became query structure rather than a string value; createObjectIds did not reject operator keys, and the resulting object reached collection.find/findOne/count/update/delete. An attacker could replace a per-user equality filter with operators such as $ne/$exists/$where, widening reads or the affected update/delete set to data accessible to the configured customer MongoDB connection.
flaw_origin: Commit f946f2f68d54e370013e28efa4cb6517067e5b18 changed packages/server/src/threads/query.js so every string field was processed with noEscaping: true. Its parent only converted a value to triple braces when the entire field matched a Handlebars expression; a quoted binding embedded in a JSON document such as {"name":"{{ name }}"} therefore remained escaped in the parent. The BIC made those embedded values raw while retaining the subsequent JSON.parse, and the already-present MongoDB integration consumed query.json directly.
ai_marker: absent — the exact BIC commit object (git cat-file commit f946f2f68d54e370013e28efa4cb6517067e5b18) names human author and committer mike12345567 <me@michaeldrury.co.uk>, contains only the issue-#4308 subject, and has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other trailer.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/Budibase/budibase/security/advisories/GHSA-pmpg-2mxq-6xwr (API: https://api.github.com/repos/Budibase/budibase/security-advisories/GHSA-pmpg-2mxq-6xwr) documents the BASIC-user POST /api/queries/:queryId path, quote-breaking payload, conversion to a MongoDB operator object, and the find/update/delete impact. It declares @budibase/server <3.40.0 affected and 3.40.0 patched; the assigned alias is https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rqxq-f5cc-3xp6 / CVE-2026-73617.

At f946f2f68d54e370013e28efa4cb6517067e5b18, packages/server/src/threads/query.js:182-188 passes every string to processStringSync with noEscaping: true; lines 193-203 then JSON.parse json/customData/requestBody. packages/server/src/integrations/mongodb.ts:108-129 already sends query.json to collection.find/findOne/findOneAndUpdate/count/distinct, establishing a complete source-to-sink path when the BIC landed.

git log -L 182,188:packages/server/src/threads/query.js at f946f2f68d54e370013e28efa4cb6517067e5b18 identifies that commit as the change replacing conditional whole-field triple-brace handling with unconditional noEscaping: true. Cross-path git -S history shows later commits 5180603374c386e4da26aaf4c4acdee32abe65ba and fc5f6ca53050ede5e7e46454808a8a00d884648f merely moved the same enrichment/parse logic into packages/server/src/integrations/queries/sql.ts and then packages/server/src/sdk/app/queries/queries.ts; they are not BICs.

Direct-parent tree verification: 86ffa65d938d80133038b85346f209d0e2fc5084:packages/server/src/threads/query.js:187-195 has the IS_HANDLEBARS/IS_TRIPLE_BRACE whole-field check and processStringSync(..., { noHelpers: true }) with no noEscaping option. The exact diff to f946f2f68d54e370013e28efa4cb6517067e5b18 removes that conditional and adds noEscaping: true. Thus the vulnerable quoted-JSON behavior is absent from the immediate parent even though JSON.parse itself already existed.

f946f2f68d54e370013e28efa4cb6517067e5b18 is the original PR member merged by 56f027e4b9dfc95fb4e52ba39940d5ddef4e0789 (PR #4313, https://github.com/Budibase/budibase/pull/4313). The later same-subject f2a025013ea034a86c841e7151c5d38cfdb6acd4 is a parallel alpha-line replay/backport: f946 has the earlier author/commit time and is the second parent of the first-party PR merge, so neither that replay nor the merge is substituted for the smallest BIC.

Introduction boundary: tag v1.0.48 resolves exactly to parent 86ffa65d938d80133038b85346f209d0e2fc5084 and does not contain the BIC; production tag v1.0.49 at 2dea8789e8e2f284c630ce7eb4b074c461fcc14a contains it. Thus the repository history narrows the advisory's open-ended <3.40.0 range on the lower side: versions before the v1.0.49 introduction are not affected by this mechanism.

Fix history: direct commit ddef68abaf823c47e1bee03a09061bae62ba6399 introduced JSON-safe parameter substitution and was merged by 33a57bd9580b54833feda3ec39f31530adba1153 (PR #18847, https://github.com/Budibase/budibase/pull/18847). 910f6d29ff38add6e04c8fe3195f0571221aa05a later reverted that merge on the development line. Durable direct commit dd8c0654b35cd89ce3645f2355f4bf2ff9a5dd80 (https://github.com/Budibase/budibase/commit/dd8c0654b35cd89ce3645f2355f4bf2ff9a5dd80) replaced raw interpolation of JSON fields with processJsonStringSync, which parses the template first and substitutes into parsed values; f30abc9fdddad33a447cfff3d1880df89e72079c added MongoDB find and updateMany quote-injection regression cases.

Release-boundary cross-check finds the public advisory conservative rather than exact: tag 3.39.5 (f33dfd3c47ebc2962a07205edb03388d005215ac) still has packages/server/src/sdk/workspace/queries/queries.ts:121-140 with noEscaping interpolation followed by JSON.parse. Tag 3.39.6 (c6bfe17485fd59e1b30cec6ba2d2a483515d0ae5) is the first numbered tag containing the initial direct fix ddef68abaf823c47e1bee03a09061bae62ba6399. Tags 3.39.6-3.39.8 retain that initial implementation; dd8c0654b35cd89ce3645f2355f4bf2ff9a5dd80 lands before 3.39.9 (a4423fc5bf237e6101c2e8348ef5372fff6484cd) and is also an ancestor of the declared patched tag 3.40.0 (661fe55d609404d073eea86702e0bde7942c3f10). No released tag occurs in the brief revert-to-dd8 interval.

A later residual invalid-JSON/multi-object MongoDB template fallback was fixed by direct commit b374d16853f0f262c21a21fb815c826cba492201, merged as 3cdd9e2f6c07ed9948fca4e751b92fb7180c13e0 (PR #19448, https://github.com/Budibase/budibase/pull/19448). That change makes each top-level filter/update document take the binding-safe path. It is absent from v3.42.0 (67de171e5934d561ea1780ef1dd0f4d0637f5bae) and present in v3.43.0 (bd8a66e31b549e102cea67c0debb68be895282c7), so the first-party 3.40.0 boundary is sufficient for its demonstrated single-object read PoC but does not describe this later-closed multi-object variant.

BIC-only attribution evidence: https://github.com/Budibase/budibase/commit/f946f2f68d54e370013e28efa4cb6517067e5b18 and the local raw commit object have a human author/committer and no AI marker. AI-related facts on fixes, PR bodies, branch names, or later commits were excluded from the attribution decision as required.
reasoning: The vulnerable sink and JSON.parse predated the BIC, but the parent escaped an embedded double-brace value and therefore did not let quote characters supplied to a normal quoted JSON binding become syntax. f946f2f68d54e370013e28efa4cb6517067e5b18 is the smallest original commit that changed that security property: it forced raw Handlebars substitution across all query string fields while the non-SQL runner continued to parse JSON and hand it to MongoDB. Later moves preserve rather than originate that mechanism, and the direct parent plus v1.0.48/v1.0.49 boundary verifies introduction. The disclosed single-object path was initially fixed in the 3.39.6 release lineage, durably reimplemented by dd8c0654b35cd89ce3645f2355f4bf2ff9a5dd80 before 3.39.9 and present in 3.40.0; a multi-object fallback variant required the later b374d16853f0f262c21a21fb815c826cba492201 change present in v3.43.0. None of those later lifecycle facts change attribution: the BIC commit object itself is human-authored with no AI marker, so the causal verdict is NOT_AI.
